D009-D001_h001.question:
"Doctor, I’m 50, and honestly, I don't even know where to begin. For the past year, I’ve been in a funk that just won't lift. It’s more than just feeling down; it’s like a persistent gray cloud. I used to be so driven, but now, even closing a big deal for my company, I feel absolutely nothing. It’s just... indifference. My mind feels foggy, too. Just trying to figure out a new business strategy, or even focusing on a conversation with my wife, and my brain just quits, utterly exhausted. Sometimes, it gets so bad, I just think, ‘I wish I wasn’t here,’ or ‘I want this all to end,’ though I'd never actually do anything. This has really affected my business; I've missed deadlines and my staff is noticing.

Then, about a month ago, it was like a switch flipped. Suddenly, I had this boundless energy. My wife said I was talking a mile a minute, jumping from one idea to another and couldn’t tolerate silence. I just felt this intense urge to keep going, unable to relax. Sleep? Who needs it? I felt fine running on just a couple of hours. I was constantly pacing, always needing to be moving, doing something. My mood was all over the place – one minute I was ecstatic, convinced I was on the verge of some brilliant breakthrough, the next I was snapping at everyone for no reason. However, this shift didn't really cause many problems; in fact, I was so productive, I caught up on some of the work I'd been neglecting.

But here’s the thing, and it’s why I finally came in. The talking fast, the racing thoughts, the trouble focusing, feeling like I can’t sit still, and even that feeling of not needing much sleep – those aren't exactly new for me. I can remember my parents and teachers complaining about how I couldn’t sit still or pay attention in school, way before I was 12. It’s always been there, just intensified the last month."
D009-D001_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D009-D001_h002.question:

I barely need any sleep, maybe two or three hours, and I still wake up feeling completely refreshed. My colleagues say I’ve been talking a mile a minute, just non-stop. Sometimes, I find myself just pacing my apartment, wringing my hands, feeling this intense restlessness. Honestly, it hasn't really impacted my work too negatively, if anything I’m getting more done.

But this is just the latest wave. Before this, for a whole year, I was in a really dark place. Just a profound sadness that wouldn't lift. Nothing brought me joy – no music, no friends, not even the satisfaction of a perfect translation. My body felt so heavy, constantly exhausted from even the slightest effort. It got so bad that I… I tried to end things, just to escape it all. That definitely interfered with everything.

The thing is, I've always been like this. Even as a kid, before I was 12, I had trouble sitting still, blurting things out, always feeling restless and talking quickly. It wasn't just during these recent ups and downs; it's always been a part of me."
D009-D001_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
